title: WorkersCloseParams
description: Parameters for the workers.close agent tool: end one of your workers. It stops the worker's process; whatever it had not finished is not finished. Reach for it when the work is done or is no longer wanted — not to retry, since a closed worker does not come back and starting another is a separate act. You can only close workers your own session started, and only while nocx still says you may.

worker.description: The worker's id, exactly as workers.spawn returned it or workers.holdings listed it.

result.title: WorkersCloseResult
result.description: What was asked of the worker, and what is left of it. Note what this does NOT say: it does not say the worker has finished. Ending its process is a request, and how it ended is a fact nocx observes for itself — ask workers.holdings for that. When the worker had a git checkout of its own, the close removed neither the checkout nor its branch, and worktree says where that checkout is and what it holds.

id.description: The worker that was asked to end.

ended.description: True when nocx asked the worker's process to stop, and true as well when it had already finished before you asked — tidying up should not have to win a race.

worktree.description: Present only when the worker had a checkout of its own: where it is, which branch it holds, and what is in it. The close removed neither the checkout nor its branch and changed nothing in it — the work there, committed or not, is intact and is yours to keep, merge, or delete. Nothing about it is cleaned up for you.

path.description: Where the checkout is on disk. It is still there: closing a worker never removes its checkout.

branch.description: The branch checked out in it, as git reports now — it may have moved since the worker was started. Empty when HEAD is detached or nothing could be read.

state.description: read: nocx asked the repository what the checkout holds, and uncommitted and ahead are its answers. unknown: the repository could not be asked — the checkout may be gone, or git failed — and uncommitted and ahead are LEFT OUT. unknown does not mean clean, and it does not fail the close: no answer here means no answer.

uncommitted.description: True when the checkout holds work no commit keeps — a tracked change or an untracked file. False when the tree is clean. Present only when state is read.

ahead.description: How many commits the branch holds beyond the commit the checkout started from — the worker's committed work, in count. Present only when state is read.
